answer:
All three fine-tuned a pretrained model on each puzzle at test time; they differed in what they pretrained and how they decoded. Scores below are from the Kaggle leaderboard, summaries from each team's writeup.

**1. NVARC (24.03)** — [writeup](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2025/writeups/nvarc)
- **Synthetic data:** They used an LLM (`gpt-oss-120b`) to mix human puzzle descriptions into new, harder ones, then generate Python programs for the input and output grids. After consistency filtering this gave about 103k synthetic puzzles.
- **Model:** They fully fine-tuned a Qwen3 4B model on 3.2M augmented samples, following the 2024 ARChitects recipe. At test time they applied per-puzzle LoRA fine-tuning, a batched depth-first search decoder, and augmentation-based rescoring of candidates.
- **Tiny Recursive Model:** A TRM ensemble was added in the last days, but it barely helped; the gain came from scaling pretraining with synthetic puzzles.

**2. the ARChitects (16.53)** — [writeup](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2025/writeups/the-architects-solution-2025)
- **Model:** They switched from their 2024 autoregressive model to a masked-diffusion LLM (LLaDA-8B) with a 2D positional encoding suited to grids.
- **Recursive refinement:** The model's output is fed back in with "soft masking" and refined over about 100 inference steps, rather than generated in one pass.
- **Supporting pieces:** A second LLaDA model predicts the output grid size, and each task gets 128 steps of test-time fine-tuning.
- **Why they switched:** Their autoregressive approach plateaued at 16.94% public, struggling with tasks that need global restructuring.

**3. MindsAI & Tufa Labs (12.64)** — [writeup](https://www.kaggle.com/competitions/arc-prize-2025/writeups/mindsai-and-tufa-labs-arc-prize-2025-solution)
- **Model:** A pruned 660M-parameter encoder–decoder derived from CodeT5-Large, pretrained for months on more than 100M reasoning examples (about 70M ARC-style).
- **Test-time adaptation:** Almost all the score comes from test-time training plus Augment–Inference–Reverse–Vote, which runs about 10k augmented inferences per task and votes on the answer. Their ablations show 8–12× gains over zero-shot.
- **Extras:** New mixup/combine augmentations, tokenizer BPE dropout, span corruption, and an ensemble of two checkpoints.

The MindsAI writeup states a private score of 15.42%, while the leaderboard listing shows 12.64; I did not resolve the discrepancy.
